record.question: Which of the following anti-anginal drug is most effective when given by sublingual route of administration?
record.explanation: Answer C: Glyceryl trinitrate (Nitroglycerine). Sublingual glyceryl trinitrate (nitroglycerin) has rapid onset and is used for prompt relief of angina. Source/context note: Acute chest pain may be an emergency; follow clinical advice and emergency protocols. Reference: https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/glyceryl-trinitrate-gtm/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
